daily-question.no-question-today: No question today. It is put together out of the catalog a few minutes after midnight; when there was not enough to build one, it tries again tomorrow.

error.it-doesn-t-exist: It doesn't exist, or your account doesn't have access to it. Admin pages need an administrator login.

map.where-the-records-are: Where the records are kept. Everyone here chose to be on this map, and chose how much of themselves it shows —
map.your-own-is-in: your own is in the profile
map.sign-in-to-see: Sign in to see where the other collectors are.
map.nobody-shares-where-they: Nobody shares where they are yet. You could be the first.

map.no-one-on-the: No one on the map yet.

blocked.signIn: The radio plays records through YouTube and Spotify. Sign in to listen — both are somebody else's player, and neither is put on the page for a visitor.
blocked.consentBefore: The radio plays records through YouTube and Spotify. Embedding either one writes its owner's storage and tells them you were here, so it takes your leave first — the bar at the bottom asks, and the
blocked.consentAfter: takes the answer back at any time.

release.this-is-the-only: This is the only pressing of the album the catalog knows.

shelf-scan.your-account-may-not: Your account may not add records to a collection yet. Ask for the collector role and the scan opens up.
shelf-scan.sign-in-as-a: Sign in as a collector to add records to your collection.

shelf-scan.an-admin-approves-each: An admin approves each request; nothing enters the catalogue before that.

joinPrompt.pitch: The catalog is open to everyone — {{albums}} albums of {{artists}} artists to read through. Sign in to keep the copies you own, see what a collection is still missing and have your shelf follow you between devices.

badgeSettings.a-collection-s-badge: A collection's badge is drawn once by an image model, from the collection's own data, and then it is fixed.
badgeSettings.switched-off-no-badge: Switched off, no badge can be drawn and nothing can be spent.
badgeSettings.the-vertex-region-not: The Vertex region — not necessarily the one the database is in.
badgeSettings.how-many-the-admin: How many the admin picks between. More costs more, and every one of them is billed.
badgeSettings.the-ceiling-for-the: The ceiling for the whole day, counted on the server. A loop that goes wrong stops here instead of on the invoice.
badgeSettings.the-style-lock-the: The style lock — the fixed sentences every badge is drawn from — and the style version live in code. They are the only reason a shelf of badges reads as one set: if a curator could edit them per badge, the set would drift apart within weeks. Changing them is a deliberate act, and it means regenerating every badge.

releaseRequestRow.not-in-the-catalog: Not in the catalog — approving creates the album too
releaseRequestRow.add-the-release-to: Add the release to the album in the admin, then link it here.

releaseRequestAdmin.pressings-the-collectors-own: Pressings the collectors own but the catalog is missing. Approving adds the release to the catalog and the copy to the collector's collection.

musicCollectionAdmin.sets-of-records-defined: Sets of records defined by a rule. What belongs to one is resolved against the catalog, so a collection grows with it — and the badge is earned by owning all of them.
musicCollectionAdmin.whoever-earned-its-badge: ? Whoever earned its badge loses it, and this cannot be undone here.

musicCollectionEdit.a-collection-is-a: A collection is a rule, not a list: what belongs to it is resolved against the catalog every time it is read.
musicCollectionEdit.name: Name
musicCollectionEdit.a-primeicons-class-as: A PrimeIcons class, as in the menu.
musicCollectionEdit.a-draft-is-not: A draft is not listed and earns nobody a badge.
musicCollectionEdit.every-filter-given-must: Every filter given must hold. A filter left empty says nothing — with all of them empty the collection asks for the whole catalog.
musicCollectionEdit.discogs-roles-comma-separated: Discogs roles, comma separated. One credit must satisfy both: the musician in that role, not two credits together.
musicCollectionEdit.without-a-name-the: Without a name the collection rewards no badge.
musicCollectionEdit.a-hand-made-image: A hand-made image, for the rare badge that wants one. The generated pin below wins over it.
musicCollectionEdit.drawn-by-an-image: Drawn by an image model, from this collection's own data. The style is the same on every badge — only the motif, the enamel, the patina and the rim follow the rule. Every image drawn is kept, so the pin can be any of them, today or next year.
musicCollectionEdit.save-the-collection-first: Save the collection first: the prompt is built on the server from what is stored, not from this form.
musicCollectionEdit.no-filter-yet-this: No filter yet — this rule takes in the whole catalog. Publishing it is refused.
musicCollectionEdit.points-and-only-once: points, and only once a collector owns every one of them. Owning the original pressing of an old record raises it further.

pointsHint.one: What finishing it is worth. Left empty the rule decides — how many records it asks for, and how old they are — which right now would be {{count}} point.
pointsHint.other: What finishing it is worth. Left empty the rule decides — how many records it asks for, and how old they are — which right now would be {{count}} points.

profilePrivacy.puts-youtube-s-and: Puts YouTube's and Spotify's players on the page. They are not ours: each one writes its own storage and tells its owner you were here. Switching it off takes them off the page at once, and the records go silent.
profilePrivacy.count-how-the-app: Count how the app is used
profilePrivacy.which-pages-and-features: Which pages and features get opened, through Google Analytics. No advertising, and nothing about your records or your searches. Switching it off stops it at once and clears what it left in this browser.

profilePlayback.show-the-lyrics-when: Show the lyrics when there are any
profilePlayback.play-on-to-the: Play on to the next track

profileShelves.draw-the-shelving-you: Draw the shelving you actually own. A unit is a grid of square compartments, so 4 × 2 stands upright and 2 × 4 is the same unit on its side. Records are filed from the first unit to the last.
profileShelves.nothing-drawn-yet-the: Nothing drawn yet — the collection stands on one open wall that grows with it.

short.one: {{count}} record has nowhere to stand — it shows below the furniture until you draw more.
short.other: {{count}} records have nowhere to stand — they show below the furniture until you draw more.

profileAppearance.the-wide-setting-only: The wide setting only shows on a screen with room to spare.

profileListening.nothing-yet-put-a: Nothing yet. Put a record on from an album page and it is counted here — a record counts once it has played for half a minute, and counts as heard right through once every track of it has been.

nextAlbums.the-moment-it-is: the moment it is on the shelf

consentBar.you-can-change-either: You can change either of these any time on your profile.

form.savingKeepsBoth: Saving keeps both — merge one away in the catalog.

dailyQuestionSettings.title: Daily question
dailyQuestionSettings.lead: The rules of the game: how long there is to answer, what a guess pays, and what the engine may ask about.
dailyQuestionSettings.switched-off: Switched off, no new question is composed and the page says so. The days already composed stay as they are.
dailyQuestionSettings.time-limit-hint: How long there is to answer. Zero takes the clock off, and with it the speed bonus. A late guess is still taken — it just pays nothing.
dailyQuestionSettings.streak-bonus-hint: The first day of a run pays no bonus: the bonus is for coming back.
dailyQuestionSettings.speed-bonus-hint: Paid on a sliding scale: all of it for an instant answer, nothing for one that used up the clock. Without a clock it pays nothing.
dailyQuestionSettings.bonus-day-chance-hint: Drawn from the day itself, so the same day is a bonus day for everybody.
dailyQuestionSettings.question-kinds-hint: What you switch off is never drawn. The material-hungry kinds switch themselves on as the data fills in — switching one off always wins.
dailyQuestionSettings.leaderboard-size-hint: Everybody else still sees their own place: the nightly run writes it into their pot.
dailyQuestionSettings.compose-exists: {{day}}: the question was already up; nothing was overwritten.
dailyQuestionSettings.compose-disabled: The game is switched off, so no question was composed.
dailyQuestionSettings.compose-no-material: There was not enough in the catalog to make a question.
dailyQuestionSettings.history-hint: What the game has been asking. The answers are not in the list — those stay on the server. The composing looks a fortnight back: it will not ask about the same album again until then, about the same kind of question for a week, or about the same artist for four days.
